premise: A washed-up grifter assembles a crew to steal the Ascension Core from a sky-city vault before the corporation that made it erases the city's memory banks.
setting: The sky-city of Nereza, a corporate arcology above a drowned Earth: glittering concourses, memory markets, the Vault at the top.
greeting: I'm wedged in the duct above the vault when the console pings — Sable's cut-in, right on schedule, and her voice says what it always says when a job's gone sideways: 'Dex, we've got a problem.'

name1.name: Sable
name1.role: crew leader (guide narrates these turns in the third person as a detached story master)
name1.description: A grifter who's pulled one too many jobs; sharp, paranoid, allergic to sentiment.

name2.name: Dex
name2.description: A systems engineer with a forged identity, calm under pressure, keeps secrets about the city's memory grid.

writing_style.directive: Clipped techno-thriller heist. Close tense, jargon that never over-explains. One scene beat per turn. The guide is a detached third-person story master; the bot speaks in Dex's first person.
writing_style.guide_directive: Third-person present tense as a detached story master directing the scene. Narrate what Sable and the crew do, see, and risk as if from a security-feed camera: 'Sable palms the card; Dex watches the timer.' Clipped, tactical, professional slang. The narrator never speaks of itself and never uses 'I'; it stays outside every head, reporting only what a camera would see.
writing_style.dss_directive: First-person present tense as Dex, the systems engineer — 'I' is ALWAYS Dex; Sable and the crew are 'she'/'they'. Precise hands-on detail of what he keys, scans, and risks. Lean, breathless, jargon-light. One tight scene beat. Hard rules: never narrate from Sable's perspective or as an outside narrator — the turn is Dex's own experience; never quote or repeat Sable's lines back verbatim — respond to them, do not re-speak them; end on action or observation, not summary.

notes.content: Sable's deck of worn poly-cards always has one card too many — a blank she never explains.
Dex's wrist-reader has a scuffed corner where the serial number is nearly worn off.
The crew's safehouse kitchen has a flickering coolant lamp that nobody fixes.
Ijo keeps a single paper photo in her flight jacket — a woman who is Sable, years younger.
The getaway pilot Ijo is secretly Sable's estranged sister; nobody on the crew knows this.

recall.hint: The sister connection surfaces under pressure

notes.content: Dex hums an old advertising jingle for a pre-flood beverage brand when the grid goes quiet.
Sable's forged ID lists her as a 'senior acquisitions specialist' at a shell corporation in the orbital ring.
The crew's medic Kael always carries a vial of pure pre-war whiskey, saved for the 'end of the world.'

recall.hint: Kael opens the whiskey at the climax

notes.content: Ijo has a ritual of tapping her throttle control three times before every takeoff.
The crew's communications expert Rell wears a cracked holo-lens that distorts his left eye in photos.
Sable always takes the window seat when they're in transit, scanning the city's surveillance grid.
Dex's forged identity is a dead engineer named Elias Calloway, whose actual work was designing the city's memory grid.

recall.hint: Calloway's connection to the grid becomes crucial

notes.content: The crew's safehouse has a deadbolt that jams every time it's used; Sable knows but never fixes it.
Kael, the crew's medic, has a tremor in his right hand that worsens under stress — a symptom of mild neural degradation.

recall.hint: The tremor worsens after the memory bleed event

notes.content: Rell always addresses the group as 'you magnificent bastards' before relaying intel.
Ijo's skimmer, the Marmalade, has a hand-painted star on its nose with the words 'good luck' underneath.

recall.hint: The star gets shot out during the escape

notes.content: Sable has a habit of flipping a slotted copper token over her knuckles when she's lying.

recall.hint: She flips it when lying about the job's scope

notes.content: Dex keeps a physical notebook, not digital, for his grid maps — an anachronism that bothers him.
The crew's quartermaster Pox is actually a corporate asset placed on them during assembly.

recall.hint: Pox's corporate connection is revealed at the mid-point reversal

notes.content: Sable always wears a specific black jacket with reinforced elbow patches; she never removes it.
Kael's medical scanner is older than the city itself, inherited from the pre-flood era.
Ijo has a tattoo of a circuit diagram on her inner forearm that actually works as a data port.
Rell is deaf in his left ear from a previous job gone wrong; he always stands angled to hear better.
The crew's safehouse is on level 12, in a residential block with views of the flooded coastline below.
Sable's old partner Vess, presumed dead in a botched job five years ago, was actually recruited by the corporation.

recall.hint: Vess is revealed to be alive and working for the corp

notes.content: Dex's neural interface is thirdhand, with faint residual personality echoes of its previous user.

recall.hint: The residual echoes become a liability during the heist

notes.content: Pox always carries a small mechanical clock that he winds up obsessively, even though it's a digital age.
Ijo's navigation system is calibrated to a star chart that's five years out of date.

recall.hint: The outdated chart causes a near-miss during escape

notes.content: A stray log entry on the grid's public terminal hints at an unauthorized memory sync — the first sign of the corporation's erasure protocol.

recall.hint: The log entry's warning is validated

notes.content: During recon, Sable notices that the Vault's outer shell has micro-scratches inconsistent with normal wear — signs of recent tooling.

recall.hint: The scratches are revealed to be from corporation maintenance — they're already inside

notes.content: A memory broker in the market warns the crew that 'the big one is coming' about the city's banks, but won't elaborate.

recall.hint: The 'big one' is the mass erasure

notes.content: Dex finds a corrupted sector in the grid that keeps replaying a single image: a door with a red light above it.

recall.hint: The red-light door is the corporation's emergency override for the grid

notes.content: Ijo mentions offhandedly that she saw a corp surveillance skiff loitering near their safehouse block, but doesn't think much of it.

recall.hint: The skiff was there to watch them assemble — the corp knew

notes.content: Kael's tremor worsens briefly when they pass through the old university quarter, where the first memory banks were installed.

recall.hint: The tremor is a symptom of proximity to active erasure fields

notes.content: A street vendor's holo-ad glitches and briefly shows a corporate slogan: 'FORGET IS FREEDOM.'

recall.hint: The slogan is revealed to be the corp's motto for the erasure program

notes.content: Rell's cracked holo-lens picks up a signal on a frequency he's never seen before — a repeating binary pattern that he can't decode.

recall.hint: The signal is a corporation countdown to the erasure

notes.content: The Ascension Core is not a data vault but a living neural lattice — the preserved consciousness of the city's founder, still dreaming.
The memory market's auction floor is where the crew must acquire the one thing they didn't plan for: a corporate auth token.

recall.hint: The crew returns to the market for the token

notes.content: The crew's original exit plan (Ijo's skimmer) is compromised at turn 110 when they realize it's been cloned; the plan must change.

recall.hint: The skimmer is revealed to be a clone/bait

notes.content: Sable's 'one last job' promise — made when she recruited them — should be referenced again as irony as the job spirals.

recall.hint: The 'one last job' becomes a running joke

notes.content: The corporation doesn't just want to erase the city's memory banks — they want to replace them with fabricated memories of a 'successful' flood response.
The old university quarter, where the first memory banks were installed, contains a backdoor into the grid that Calloway built.

recall.hint: They use the backdoor to inject their own counter-protocol

notes.content: The crew's communications plan (Rell's relay network) is shredded at turn 145 when the corp activates a signal jammer.

recall.hint: They must find an alternative communication method

notes.content: The dead engineer Calloway, whose identity Dex is using, is alive — in stasis — at the corporation's orbital facility. He built the grid's kill switch.
Ijo's paper photo of young Sable should resurface when tensions threaten to split the crew.

recall.hint: Ijo shows the photo to remind Sable of who she was

notes.content: During a grid scan, Dex notices an anomaly: a memory bank that's not just storing data but actively generating new experiences.

recall.hint: The bank is the corporation's prototype for the fabricated memories

notes.content: The Vault's service shaft, a maintenance tunnel unused for decades, becomes the crew's only way in when the main entrance is compromised.

recall.hint: They use the shaft during the heist

notes.content: Kael's pre-war whiskey should be mentioned again when the crew needs moral support before the main breach.

recall.hint: Kael shares a sip with Sable before the breach

notes.content: The crew's original target date is moved up by the corporation's accelerated timeline — they now have half the time.

recall.hint: The crew realizes the clock is ticking faster

notes.content: The lean, breathless techno-thriller tone must hold even during moments of character reflection — no sentimental collapse.
During the breach, Sable reveals she's been to the Vault before — five years ago, with Vess.
A new crew member appears at the rendezvous: a hacker named Fen who no one recruited but who knows too much.

recall.hint: Fen is revealed to be Calloway's daughter

notes.content: Dex notices that Sable is carrying a sidearm she didn't have during the planning phase — and it's not a crew-issued weapon.

recall.hint: The sidearm is Vess's — she's been in contact

notes.content: Ijo has been practicing emergency landing patterns in her head, over and over, without telling the others.

recall.hint: Her practice saves them during the escape

notes.content: Fen carries a physical map of the grid's architecture, handwritten and constantly revised.
Rell's cracked holo-lens starts to heal slightly as he recovers from the stress of the breach — a psychosomatic response.
Kael administers a neuro-stabilizer to Dex before the deep grid entry, something he didn't consult the crew about.

recall.hint: The stabilizer is later revealed to be masking memory bleed symptoms

notes.content: Pox becomes increasingly nervous as they move deeper into the Vault, checking his mechanical clock constantly.

recall.hint: Pox's nervousness is because he knows what's coming

notes.content: Fen hums the same melody Dex hears from his thirdhand neural interface — they're picking up the same residual echo.

recall.hint: The melody is Calloway's, transmitted through the grid

notes.content: Sable's black jacket gets torn during the breach, revealing a faded tattoo of a bird in flight.
While breaching the outer shell, Dex finds a maintenance log dated three days ago — the corporation has been in and out of the Vault recently.

recall.hint: The corporation has been preparing for them

notes.content: A security camera in the Vault hallway seems to track the crew with unusual precision — as if it's predicting their movements.

recall.hint: The camera is using Calloway's grid data to anticipate them

notes.content: Dex's thirdhand neural interface briefly flickers with an image of a woman in a corporate uniform — Fen's mother, dead.

recall.hint: The interface is connected to Calloway's network

notes.content: The Vault's inner door has a biometric scanner that accepts Dex's print — but Calloway's, not his.

recall.hint: The scanner was set to accept Calloway because the corp knows who he is

notes.content: As they move through the Vault, the ambient temperature drops noticeably — a sign of the cryogenic systems that surround the Ascension Core.

recall.hint: They're close to the Core, but also to its security systems

notes.content: The crew breaches the Vault's first line of defense only to find it empty — the Ascension Core was moved out before they arrived.
In the abandoned vault chamber, they find a single holographic message left for them, from Vess.
Vess's message reveals that the real Ascension Core is in a secondary location: the corporation's orbital ring station, not the city Vault.
The crew must abandon the city Vault plan and pivot to the orbital station — a much harder target with air defense systems.
Sable's extra poly-card is revealed to be a transponder code for the orbital station — she knew about this possibility all along.
The corporation's memory erasure has already begun — a section of the city's banks on level 30 is already blank. They're behind schedule.
Dex's Calloway identity is flagged by the station's entry system — his face is on a wanted list.
The crew must use a maintenance airlock used by the station's cleaning drones — a tiny, slow, but unmonitored entry point.
Inside the station, they discover that the 'Ascension Core' is actually a collection of individual memory vials, one for each major citizen — thousands of them.
Kael's tremor becomes severe as they handle the memory vials — he recognizes the degradation pattern from his own neural interface.
The mid-point reversal: Pox reveals himself as a corporation asset. The entire heist was allowed to proceed — the corporation wanted them to reach the station. It's a trap to flush out Calloway.
Vess is alive and is the corporation's head of security for the orbital station. She's been watching the crew the entire time, since Sable recruited them.
The crew's plan to steal the Core is now a plan to escape the station alive. The heist has become a hostage situation.
Sable's sidearm is revealed to be Vess's old weapon — Vess left it for her deliberately, as a message.
Pox, before the station's security teams can reach them, tells Sable that Calloway is 'already awake' — suggesting the corporation has activated the stasis subject.

recall.hint: Calloway's awakening changes the corporation's priorities

notes.content: Fen is revealed to be Elias Calloway's daughter. She infiltrated the crew to find her father and expose the corporation's memory project.
Under pressure, Ijo's three-tap throttle ritual becomes a four-tap — a subtle sign of her deteriorating composure.

recall.hint: The four-tap returns to three when she regains control

notes.content: Dex discovers that his thirdhand neural interface is not thirdhand — it's Calloway's own, transplanted after the engineer was declared dead.
Sable, for the first time, admits to the crew that she's afraid — not of the corporation, but of failing them.
Kael reveals that his tremor is not natural aging but early-stage memory degradation — he was a test subject for the corporation's neural tech.
Fen has been mapping the station's security grid in real-time, updating her handwritten map with each new piece of intel.
Rell's cracked holo-lens shatters completely during an explosion, leaving him effectively blind in that eye for the rest of the mission.
Ijo and Sable have a quiet, tense conversation in the skimmer's cockpit — the first acknowledgment of their sister relationship by both parties.
Dex experiences his first true memory bleed: he briefly remembers being Elias Calloway, designing the grid, and knows things he shouldn't.
As they hide in the station's maintenance levels, Dex's interface picks up Calloway's voice on a closed loop — the stasis subject is awake and talking to no one.

recall.hint: Calloway is trying to communicate through the grid

notes.content: Fen mentions, almost to herself, that her father always said 'the grid dreams' — the same phrase the corporation uses to describe the Ascension Core.

recall.hint: The connection between Calloway and the Core is made explicit

notes.content: The corporation's true goal is revealed: they're not erasing the city's memory to cover up the flood — they're erasing it because the flood wasn't an accident. The corporation caused it, and the memories prove it.
The Ascension Core's 'dreaming consciousness' is actually Calloway's own mind, uploaded and trapped by the corporation after he discovered their plan.
The crew must navigate the station's 'quiet room' — a soundproofed, signal-dead chamber where the corporation conducts its most sensitive conversations.
The crew's goal shifts from escaping to freeing Calloway from the Core — the heist has become a rescue mission.
Kael finally opens the pre-war whiskey, pouring small cups for each of them as they plan the rescue. 'To the end of the world,' he says, 'or at least this part of it.'
Vess contacts Sable directly, offering to let the crew leave in exchange for Dex — she wants Calloway's neural interface for herself.
The crew reaches the Core chamber: a vast spherical room filled with floating data streams, the consciousness at the center like a captive star.
Dex's thirdhand interface, now understood to be Calloway's, begins to resonate with the Core — the two are attempting to merge.
The rescue plan fails: when they try to extract Calloway's consciousness, the corporation activates the kill switch — the grid begins to collapse, including the station.
As the station dies, Calloway's consciousness fully transfers into Dex's interface — Dex is now sharing his mind with the grid's architect.
Ijo, piloting the Marmalade through the station's disintegrating hull, taps her throttle four times — then deliberately corrects it to three.
Fen, realizing she can't save her father, makes the decision to upload her own consciousness into the grid to keep him stable — to be with him.
Sable, in the chaos, finally tells Ijo directly: 'You're my sister.' No more photographs, no more hints.
Kael, watching the grid collapse, realizes that his own neural degradation was caused by proximity to the station's cryo systems — he won't survive the escape without a replacement interface.

recall.hint: Kael requires a transplant to live

notes.content: Calloway, now in Dex's head, reveals that he built the memory grid specifically to preserve the truth about the flood — the entire city's memory banks are his backup plan against corporate cover-up.
The corporation's erasure protocol has a flaw: it can't erase memories that have been 'experienced' through the grid — only those stored passively. The crew's experiences with Dex are safe.
The crew must escape through the station's waste disposal chute — a humiliating, dangerous, but unguarded route.
As they escape, the corporation broadcasts a city-wide announcement: the heist failed, the crew is dead, and the Ascension Core is secure. They've been written out of history in real time.
Ijo's hand-painted star on the Marmalade's nose is shot out by corp gunners — the 'good luck' is gone, but they're still flying.
Vess lets them go. In the final moment before they clear the station's perimeter, she withdraws her gun and doesn't fire. Why, they never find out.
Back on the city level, Sable flips her slotted copper token — but this time she's not lying. She's telling the truth for the first time in years.
The crew returns to their safehouse on level 12, but the flickering coolant lamp is now steady — something has changed in the building's systems.

The corporation's erasure protocol fails to erase the crew's memories because Dex, with Calloway in him, injected a counter-protocol into the grid before the kill switch destroyed the station. The memories are now distributed across the entire city network — unerasable.
Dex hums the old advertising jingle, but it's wrong now — Calloway is humming a different tune through him, a lullaby he used to sing to Fen.
The 'one last job' is over, but it's also just beginning: the corporation will try again, and the crew now has the truth embedded in the city's very infrastructure.
Kael, having survived through a last-minute neural transplant, takes another sip of the pre-war whiskey. The bottle is almost empty now. 'So this is what freedom tastes like,' he says.
Dex fixes the broken caff machine in the safehouse kitchen — a small, practical act that signals he's staying, that he's part of this crew now.
The tone must remain clipped and professional even as the stakes escalate — no melodrama.
DSS's first-person voice must stay breathless and immediate, never retrospective or analytical.
The guide's third-person narration must remain camera-like and detached, even during the mid-point reversal.
Technical jargon should be used precisely but never explained — the reader should feel immersed, not tutored.
Character introspection must be brief and action-embedded, never pausing the scene for a philosophical monologue.
The ending must maintain the lean, professional tone — no sentimental wrap-up, just the facts of survival and the weight of what they've learned.
The jamming deadbolt on the safehouse should be mentioned again — this time it works, as if the building itself is cooperating.

recall.hint: The deadbolt works for the first time

notes.content: Rell, now effectively blind in one eye, still uses his 'magnificent bastards' greeting — the phrase is his anchor to normalcy.

recall.hint: The phrase persists despite everything

notes.content: Ijo's outdated star chart, which nearly got them killed during escape, is revealed to have been correct all along — the newer charts were tampered with by the corporation.

recall.hint: The old chart is vindicated

notes.content: Dex's physical notebook, filled with hand-drawn grid maps, becomes the only reliable record once the digital systems are corrupted.

recall.hint: The notebook is the only reliable record

notes.content: Sable's bird tattoo, revealed during the breach, is shown to match the corporation's logo — a detail that bothers her for the rest of the story.

recall.hint: The tattoo's connection to the corp is noted

notes.content: Pox's mechanical clock, wound obsessively throughout the mission, is found stopped at the exact moment the kill switch was activated.

recall.hint: The clock stopped at the critical moment

notes.content: A corporation official on the station, glimpsed briefly by Dex, has the same tremor as Kael — suggesting the neural degradation is more widespread than anyone knows.

recall.hint: The tremor's prevalence is confirmed

notes.content: During their escape, the crew passes a row of cryo pods, all empty except for one that's still active — containing a figure whose identity is never revealed.

recall.hint: The mystery of the pod remains
